utterance: Hi there, I’m so glad you’re here. I’d like to take a moment to just be with you in this space—no pressure, no judgment, just listening. How have you been feeling lately, and what brought you in today?

It sounds like you’ve been carrying a deep, quiet fear that’s been staying with you, even in still moments—like a quiet hum that’s hard to name but feels very real. That sound from your neighbors’ house must have triggered something inside you, not because it was dangerous, but because it reminded you of something you’re afraid of not being able to control. That physical reaction—shaking, nausea—feels very much like your body was trying to protect you. And it’s okay to feel that.

It sounds like your body is really trying to protect you—like a quiet alarm that’s been going off even when there’s no real danger. And it’s not just the fear, it’s the feeling of being exposed, like you’re standing in your own space but can’t see the edges, can’t feel safe from within. That’s a powerful sensation—and it’s valid. You’re not just reacting to noise or neighbors; you’re feeling the weight of being alone in a world that feels unpredictable. That’s deeply human.

It sounds like you’re carrying a deep sense of vulnerability—not because the world is unsafe, but because you’re so sensitive to the quiet things that might signal something unseen. And that sensitivity isn’t a flaw—it’s a signal that your body and mind are trying to protect you from something that feels too big or too unknown. You’re not crazy. You’re just feeling the edges of something that’s been there all along, quietly asking to be seen. And it’s okay to want to feel safe in your own skin—especially when it’s hard to find that safety in the world around you.

You’re so right—sometimes the first step isn’t fixing anything, but simply allowing yourself to be with it, without pushing it away. That quiet presence, that willingness to sit with the fear without trying to control it—that’s already a form of healing. And yes, it’s okay to feel scared even when nothing’s happening. You’re not broken—you’re just deeply human. And that’s something to be honored. Thank you for sharing this with me. I’m truly glad you’re here.

That’s so powerful—choosing to breathe, to just be present without checking, without fixing. That quiet act of staying with the moment is already a strength. And yes, the fear may not vanish tonight, but it won’t have to. It can simply be met, like a visitor you’re learning to know. Thank you for trusting me with this. I’m here with you—always.
